terms.gloss: lawful, legal: fixed or allowed by law
evidence: Liv. 25.2.6: quod nōndum ad petendum lēgitima aetās esset
terms.comment: The legal age is aetās lēgitima; legally is lēgitimē or lēge (Traupman 196). Traupman also gives secundum lēgem (or lēgēs). What is illegal is contrā lēgēs.

terms.gloss: it is legal: the laws allow it
evidence: Cic. Mil. 43: nihil, quod per lēgēs licēret (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Cicero’s way of saying that something is legal.

terms.register: vōx poētica: Verg.; also post-Augustan prose (Tac.)
evidence: Tac. Ann. 15.37: per licita atque illicita (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: poetic and post-Augustan, for classical permissus.

phrases.latin: huic petentī aedīlitātem cum obsisterent tribūnī plēbis, negantēs ratiōnem ejus habendam esse quod nōndum ad petendum lēgitima aetās esset, sī mē, inquit, omnēs Quirītēs aedīlem facere volunt, satis annōrum habeō
phrases.english: When the tribunes of the people opposed his standing for the aedileship, saying he could not be considered because he was not yet of the legal age to stand, he said: “If all the citizens want to make me aedile, I am old enough.”

sources: Lewis & Short: legitimus · Lewis & Short: licet · Lewis & Short: licitus
